# Metropolis Ascendant - Full Bonus List

*Auto-generated from the mod's data, so it matches the in-game node notes exactly.*

Every Metropolis Ascendant bonus, grouped by source. The Ascendancy civic-tree entries below are the exact text shown on each node's in-game panel, so this list can't drift from what you see in-game. Bonuses pay out across all your Settlements while your footprint stays within your earned allowance - you start with one Settlement and earn Charters to widen it, up to four - and switch off if you exceed it.

## The Ascendancy Tree

*Your metropolis researches its own civic tree - three roots, deepening masteries and a repeatable capstone, re-keyed to every Age. Each node's Boost (a goal that, once met, makes that node research faster - the Civ VI boost idea) is listed with it. Text below is exactly what the node's in-game panel shows.*

### Antiquity

- **Muses** (Culture): +1 Culture per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements. +1 Culture on each building with a Quarter or Wonder adjacency bonus.
  - Boost: Build a Monument.
- **Monument Builders** (Culture): +1 Culture per 2 Urban Population in Joyous Settlements, +1 more per 2 in Ecstatic Settlements. +10% Production toward Wonders.
  - Mastery: +1 more Culture on each building with a Quarter or Wonder adjacency bonus, and +1 Specialist capacity in each Settlement.
  - Boost: Build a Wonder.
- **Homesteads** (Growth): +2 Food in each of your Settlements. +2 Food on each food building next to a Mountain or Natural Wonder.
  - Boost: Have 3 Farms.
- **Fertile Valleys** (Growth): Whenever a Settlement adds a rural tile - through growth or purchase - gain +3 Food per Rural Population there. +1 more Food on each food building next to a Mountain or Natural Wonder (+3 total).
  - Mastery: the frontier's slopes give more - +2 Production on each food building next to a Mountain or Natural Wonder.
  - Boost: Grow a Settlement to 10 total Population.
- **Musters** (Military): Your metropolis fortifies itself: +25 Health on your Districts, +5 Healing per turn for your units, and +1 Gold on each Fortification. Unlocks two Traditions: Spoils of Knowledge (Science from defeated enemy units, up to a cap) and Esprit de Corps (Combat Strength that rises with your metropolis's Happiness).
  - Boost: Train 3 infantry units.
- **Workshops** (Infrastructure): +1 Production per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements.
  - Boost: Build a Brickyard or a Saw Pit.
- **Caravans** (Trade): +1 Gold per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements. +1 Trade Route.
  - Boost: Have 2 Resources assigned in one Settlement.
- **The Spice Roads** (Trade): +2 Gold for each different Resource type assigned in your empire. +1 Trade Route. +5 Trade Route range. +1 Happiness per Resource assigned in each Settlement.
  - Mastery: +2 Resource capacity in each Settlement (+3 in Modern), and +1 Specialist capacity in each Settlement.
  - Boost: Have 2 Trade Routes.
- **Scribes** (Science): +1 Science per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements. +1 Science on each building with a Quarter, Wonder, or Resource adjacency bonus.
  - Boost: Build a Library.
- **House of Scrolls** (Science): +1 Science per 2 Urban Population in Joyous Settlements, +1 more per 2 in Ecstatic Settlements. +3 Great Work slots on your Palace and +2 on each building with a Great Work slot.
  - Mastery: +1 more Science on each building with a Quarter, Wonder, or Resource adjacency bonus, and +1 Specialist capacity in each Settlement.
  - Boost: Display 2 Codices.
- **Envoys** (Diplomacy): +2 Influence per turn.
  - Boost: Be Suzerain of a City-State.
- **Covenants** (Diplomacy): Your City-State streams deepen: for each City-State type you are Suzerain of, your cities earn +1 of its yield per 3 Urban Population, up from per 4.
  - Mastery: +1 Resource capacity in each Settlement for every City-State you are Suzerain of.
  - Boost: Be Suzerain of 2 City-States.
- **Crossroads** (Economy): +1 Production per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements.
  - Boost: Build a Market and a Garden together on one tile.
- **Rites of Ascendancy** (Culture, repeatable): +1 Culture on each building with a Quarter or Wonder adjacency bonus. Each completion permanently grants +1 Culture and +1 Gold in every Settlement.

## Civic Boosts

Every civic on the tree carries a Boost - a goal shown on the node (listed with each node above). Meet it and that civic researches faster: a reward for playing with intent, in the spirit of Civilization VI's tech and civic boosts. Boosted nodes are flagged on the tree and in the dashboard.

## Feats & Dedications

**Major feats** - each earns a Triumph whose rewards are granted IMMEDIATELY (a Tradition with an extra slot, a bonus package, an immediate +1 settlement allowance, or a next-Age Dedication - the in-game Triumph text states the exact effects):
- **The First Academy** (Antiquity Science): Build a Library and an Academy together on one tile.
- **The Athenaeum** (Exploration Science): Have a district with 80 or more total Yield.
- **The Grand Symposium** (Modern Science): Complete 6 Masteries.
- **The Wonder Crown** (Antiquity Culture): Have 3 Wonders on tiles adjacent to your Amphitheater.
- **Arcadian Idyll** (Exploration Culture): Own 10 Breathtaking rural tiles.
- **The Perfected Quarter** (Modern Culture): Build a Museum and an Opera House together on one tile.
- **The Merchant Compact** (Antiquity Economy): Build the Emporium of an Economic City-State.
- **Coin and Canvas** (Exploration Economy): Have 6 Trade Routes.
- **All Goods Under Heaven** (Modern Economy): Have 15 Resources assigned in one Settlement.
- **Delenda Est** (Antiquity Expansion): Capture an enemy settlement and raze it.
- **Twin Capitals** (Exploration Expansion): Grow your Distant Lands settlement into a City.
- **The Contented Empire** (Modern Expansion): Have every Settlement Ecstatic at the same time, with at least 2 Settlements.
- **The Open Court** (Antiquity Diplomacy): Be Suzerain of 2 different types of City-State.
- **The Great Protector** (Exploration Diplomacy): Be the first to hold Suzerainty of 3 different types of City-State.
- **Primus Inter Pares** (Modern Diplomacy): Be Suzerain of 4 different types of City-State at the same time.

**Allowance slots** - one per Age, granted IMMEDIATELY on earning that Age's Expansion feat - no tree, no research step; each permanently raises your settlement allowance by 1. Floors (free): Antiquity 1, Exploration/Modern 2. Max per Age: Antiquity 2, Exploration 3, Modern 4 - the Exploration slot carries into Modern automatically, and Modern's own Expansion feat opens the 4th.
- **Settlers' Charter** (Antiquity): +1 settlement allowance, up to 2. +1 Settlement Limit.
- **Royal Charter** (Exploration): +1 settlement allowance, up to 3. +1 Settlement Limit.
- **Homestead Act** (Modern): +1 settlement allowance, up to 4 (with your Exploration slot carried). +1 Settlement Limit.

**Dedications** - carry your legacy into the next Age:
- **Delenda Est**: Begin the Age with 500 Gold and 200 Influence.
- **Twin Capitals**: Each of your Distant Lands Settlements gains 5 Population.
- **The Great Protector**: +25% efficiency toward Befriending and becoming Suzerain of City-States this Age.

## Traditions

*Every card this mod adds is a Tradition you slot into your government - there are no separate Policies.*

**Tradition cards** - unlocked on their Ascendancy tree node; each Age brings its own:
- **Scholars' Stipend**: +1 Science per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **Festival Days**: +1 Culture per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **Market Tolls**: +1 Gold per 2 Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **Land Stewards**: +1 Food per 2 Rural Population in all your Settlements.
- **Concordat**: +1/2/3 (by Age) Influence per turn for each different type of City-State you are Suzerain of.
- **Silks and Spices**: +1/2/3 (by Age) Happiness in each Settlement for every active Trade Route you run.
- **Spoils of Knowledge**: Gain Science equal to the strength of enemy units you defeat, up to a cap.
- **Esprit de Corps**: +2 Combat Strength for your units. +2 more while your metropolis is Joyous, and +2 more while it is Ecstatic.
- **Forges Before Fields**: +1 Production per 2 Urban Population, but -1 Food per Specialist in all your Settlements.

**Major reward Traditions** - earned from the Major feats; unlike the node cards above, these carry across the Age transition and stack:
- **Alma Mater**: +5 Science on each tile that holds both a Library and an Academy. (Exploration: +5 Science on each tile that holds both a University and an Observatory. Modern: +5 Science on each tile that holds both a Schoolhouse and a Laboratory.)
- **Grand Academy**: +1 Science per Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **Omniscience**: +1 Science per Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **Crown of Wonders**: +2 Culture on each Wonder you own.
- **City Beautiful**: +2 Culture and +1 Happiness on each Breathtaking tile you own.
- **The Counting House**: +1 Gold per Urban Population in your Capital. +1 Resource capacity in your Capital.
- **Golden Age of Trade**: +2 Gold per Urban Population in your Capital. +2 Resource capacity in your Capital.
- **The World Exchange**: +2 Gold for each different Resource type assigned in your empire. +2 Resource capacity in your Capital.
- **League of Peoples**: +2 Culture in your Capital for each City-State you are Suzerain of.
- **Pax Metropolitana**: +2 Happiness in each Settlement for every City-State you are Suzerain of.
- **Magnum Opus**: +1 Culture per Urban Population in all your Settlements.
- **The Long Peace**: +1 Food, Production, Gold, Science and Culture per 2 Urban Population in each Ecstatic Settlement.

## Custom Pantheons

*Beliefs added to the base pantheon chooser, each with its own icon:*
- **Goddess of the Plantation**: +1 Culture on Plantations in Settlements with an Altar.
- **Mistress of the Beasts**: +1 Happiness and +1 Production on Pastures and Camps in Settlements with an Altar.

## Wonders & Arcadia

*Concentrate your Wonders and natural beauty into one city - an edge a sprawling AI empire can't match, because it spreads them thin across dozens of settlements.*

- Wonders enrich the city: each Building next to a Wonder gains +1 Happiness, and your Wonders raise the Appeal of the surrounding land. (Active while tall.)
- Discover a Natural Wonder to awaken Arcadia - an exploration unlock, not a tech. Then, while tall:
- Breathtaking rural tiles each gain +1 / +2 / +3 (by Age) Culture, Production, Happiness, Science and Food.
- Every Building and Wonder gains +1 / +2 / +3 (by Age) Culture and Gold for each adjacent Mountain.
- Mountains become workable - terrace a peak and it yields the full +1 / +2 / +3 Arcadia set (Culture, Production, Happiness, Science, Food). In Exploration and Modern a Breathtaking peak stacks both the rural and mountain bonuses.
- Water becomes bounty - every worked water tile yields by type (Navigable Rivers, Minor Rivers, Lakes, the open sea, Reefs and water Natural Wonders each give their own mix of Food, Gold, Science, Culture or Happiness, more in later Ages), and Buildings near Coast or a Navigable River gain Gold / Production. In Exploration you may work the open ocean, and a coastal city gains a flat Food / Production floor just for being on the sea - so a tile-starved island metropolis can still thrive.

## Foundations

Always on, no research needed: bonus Happiness and reduced specialist upkeep that grow with your city, plus +3 Influence per turn to help you win your first city-states.

## Tall Resource Reach - the Surveyor

A small footprint shouldn't cost you resources. Build a Surveyor in any Age to claim a resource tile up to 5 tiles from your Settlements into your metropolis - spent after a single claim, so one dense city can command resources a wide empire would spread across many. The resource keeps its normal yields; the power is the reach itself.

## Raze What You Can't Hold

*A single dominant city can't keep the settlements it conquers, so razing becomes a real tool - tied to the tall playstyle, so a sprawling conquer-and-keep empire gains none of it.*

- Take a city by force: a one-time burst of +200 / +400 / +600 (by Age) Gold and +50 / +100 / +150 Influence the moment you capture it.
- Sack before you burn: your units earn +10 Gold and +10 Science on top of the base plunder for each building they pillage - a large city is worth far more to sack than a small town.
- Razing is near-instant - a city you can't hold is gone in a turn or two. While it burns it counts as a second settlement, so your tall bonuses briefly pause until it's razed (a short-term price for erasing a rival). Razing still turns other leaders against you.
